items.title: Section: The Seven Marks of the Light-Affliction Practitioner Close

items.zh: 現法資糧者，謂於今世有善法欲、諸根成熟、具戒律儀及根律儀，如前廣說。多清淨信者，謂於大師所無惑無疑，深生淨信及以勝解。如於大師，於法、於學亦復如是。其餘廣說，如前應知。成就聰慧者，謂由此故，於法於義速能領受；經久遠時，於法於義能無忘失，於法於義速能通達。具諸福德者，謂由此故，形色端嚴，眾所樂見，發清淨信，無病長壽，言辭敦肅，具大宗葉，眾所知識，成就大福，多獲衣等諸資生具，為諸國王及大臣等供養、恭敬、尊重、讚嘆。具諸功德者：謂本性成就極少欲等種種功德。如前所說沙門莊嚴、應知其相。如是等類、應知是名諸薄塵行補特伽羅行相差別。
items.en: The provision within this present life is having, in this very life, wholesome aspiration, mature faculties, and both precept-discipline and sense-restraint-discipline fully in place, as explained at length before. Abundant pure faith is generating, regarding the Teacher, deep pure faith and resolute understanding free of confusion and doubt — and likewise regarding the teaching and the training. Accomplished intelligence is swiftly grasping the teaching and its meaning, retaining them without forgetting across a long span of time, and swiftly penetrating them. Possession of merit is having a dignified and pleasing form that others delight to see, inspiring pure faith in them, together with good health, longevity, and dignified, courteous speech. Possession of virtue is having, by one's very nature, wanting little and every other such virtue as already explained among the ornaments of the renunciant. All of these together should be known as the distinguishing marks of the practitioner of naturally light affliction.

items.title: Section: Synonyms for the Practitioner Open — Topic Fourteen

items.zh: 云何補特伽羅異門？謂有六種。何等為六？一、沙門，二、婆羅門，三、梵行，四、苾芻，五、精勤，六、出家。第一沙門復有四種。何等為四？一、勝道沙門，二、說道沙門，三、活道沙門，四、壞道沙門。
items.en: What are the synonyms for a practitioner? There are six: renunciant, brāhmaṇa, one who practises the holy life, monk, the diligent one, and one gone forth from home. The first, renunciant, is itself of four kinds. What are the four? The renunciant of superior attainment, the renunciant who teaches the path, the renunciant who lives by the path, and the renunciant who corrupts the path.

items.title: The Four Renunciants, Strictly and Broadly Defined

items.zh: 當知諸善逝，名勝道沙門；諸說正法者，名說道沙門；諸修善行者，名活道沙門；諸行邪行者，名壞道沙門。諸善逝者，謂已證得貪瞋癡等無餘永盡。說正法者，謂為調伏貪瞋癡等，宣說正法。修善行者，謂為調伏貪瞋癡等，勤修正行。行邪行者，謂犯尸羅，行諸惡法。又學無學名勝道沙門。以無漏道摧滅一切見、修所斷諸煩惱故。若無如來及諸菩薩，為菩提故勤修正行，諸聲聞眾持三藏者，名說道沙門。任持世俗法毘奈耶，轉正法眼令不斷故。若諸異生補特伽羅，其性調善，為自利益勤修正行，有羞有悔，愛樂正學，為得未得、為觸未觸、為證未證勤修加行，有力有能堪得未得、堪觸未觸、堪證未證，名活道沙門。由彼現有諸善法煗，堪能生長聖慧命根，名活，非死，是故名為活道沙門。若諸犯戒補特伽羅，多行惡法，廣說乃至實非梵行自稱梵行，名壞道沙門。由彼破壞最初所有正道根本，無力無能，非生道器。雖現前有說正道教，及現前有證正道者，而彼不得，是故名為壞道沙門。
items.en: Know that the well-gone ones are called renunciants of superior attainment; those who teach the true dharma are called renunciants who teach the path; those who cultivate wholesome conduct are called renunciants who live by the path; and those of deviant conduct are called renunciants who corrupt the path. Further, both trainees and those beyond training are called renunciants of superior attainment, since both destroy, through the undefiled path, every affliction abandoned at the paths of seeing and cultivation. Where there is no Tathāgata or bodhisattva present, those disciples who, for the sake of awakening, diligently cultivate correct conduct and uphold the three baskets are called renunciants who teach the path. Any ordinary being of gentle, well-disciplined nature, diligently applying effort for the sake of attaining what is not yet attained, touching what is not yet touched, and realising what is not yet realised, is called a renunciant who lives by the path. Any who violate discipline, engaging in much unwholesome conduct — up to falsely claiming to practise the holy life while not truly doing so — is called a renunciant who corrupts the path.

items.title: Section: Only the Buddha's Teaching Contains These Four

items.zh: 世尊依彼作如是說：此初沙門，廣說乃至第四沙門，於外沙門、婆羅門教空無所有。若於是處，八支聖道安立可得；即於是處有初沙門，廣說乃至第四沙門。
items.en: Relying on this, the Bhagavān spoke thus: this first renunciant, and so on through the fourth renunciant, are utterly absent from the teachings of outside renunciants and brāhmaṇas. Wherever the eightfold noble path can genuinely be established, there too the first renunciant, and so on through the fourth renunciant, are found.

items.title: Brāhmaṇa and Holy-Life Practitioner, Each in Three Kinds

items.zh: 第二婆羅門復有三種。一、種姓婆羅門，二、名想婆羅門，三、正行婆羅門。種姓婆羅門者，謂若生在婆羅門家，從母產門之所生出，父母圓備，名婆羅門。名想婆羅門者，謂諸世間，由想等想，假立言說，名婆羅門。正行婆羅門者，謂所作事決定究竟，已能驅擯惡不善法。如說：當知婆羅門，更無有所作；所作事已辨，是謂婆羅門。第三梵行復有三種。一、受遠離梵行，二、暫時斷梵行，三、畢竟斷梵行。受遠離梵行者，謂能受學遠離一切行非梵行習婬欲法。暫時斷梵行者，謂諸異生，由世間道離欲界欲。畢竟斷梵行者，謂諸聖者得不還果，復得最上阿羅漢果。
items.en: The second, brāhmaṇa, is of three kinds: brāhmaṇa by caste, brāhmaṇa in name only, and brāhmaṇa of true conduct. As it is said: know that a true brāhmaṇa has nothing further to be done; that what was to be done is already accomplished — this is what is meant by brāhmaṇa. The third, holy-life practitioner, is of three kinds: undertaking abstention, temporary cessation, and final cessation. Final cessation is: noble ones who have attained the fruit of non-returning, and further attained the supreme fruit of arhatship.

blocks.text: The fourteenth question: what are the synonyms for a practitioner? Each name is examined and redefined.
"Wholesome aspiration, mature faculties, and both precept-discipline and sense-restraint in place." These are the seven marks of the lightly afflicted.
Renunciant (śramaṇa), brahmin, practitioner of the holy life, monk (bhikṣu), the diligent one, one gone forth.

"The well-gone ones are renunciants of superior attainment; those who teach the true Dharma are renunciants who teach the path; those who cultivate wholesome qualities are renunciants who live by the path; those who violate discipline are renunciants who defile the path." Venerable Miào Jìng: 逝 means "going": the Buddha has gone well. "Wherever the eightfold path can be established, there too the four renunciants are found"; in other teachings they are absent.

Three kinds of brahmin: by caste, in name only, by true conduct. Master Cháng Bǎi: strictly, only the one who has cut afflictions is a true brahmin (compare Day 149). The holy life is "undertaking abstention, temporary cessation, and final cessation". Master Cháng Bǎi: keeping precepts is itself the holy life.

quiz.q: There are six "異門," rendered "synonyms." How does Venerable Miào Jìng read 異門?
options: different people described from different standpoints
quiz.why: "What are the synonyms for a practitioner? There are six." Venerable Miào Jìng: from different standpoints, different people are described — all kinds of different people. The English "synonyms" and the note treat the six as names for one person; the lecture reads them as different kinds of people.

quiz.q: Who is the renunciant of superior attainment, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "well-gone"?
options: the well-gone ones; 逝 is going — going well to a fine place
quiz.why: "Know that the well-gone ones are called renunciants of superior attainment." Venerable Miào Jìng: 逝 means going — going to another place; going well, arriving at a fine place, is "well-gone."

quiz.q: Why are discipline-violators called "renunciants who corrupt the path," according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: discipline is the root of the path; without it, the path has no root and cannot arise
quiz.why: "Any who violate discipline, engaging in much unwholesome conduct — up to falsely claiming to practise the holy life while not truly doing so — is called a renunciant who corrupts the path." Venerable Miào Jìng: keeping discipline is the root of the noble path; without it the path has no root and cannot arise — hence "corrupting the path."

quiz.q: The Buddha said the four renunciants are absent outside his teaching. Why does Master Cháng Bǎi say even the path-corrupter is absent there?
options: only where there is a true path can it be corrupted; outsiders lack the eightfold path
quiz.why: "Wherever the eightfold noble path can genuinely be established, there too the first renunciant, and so on through the fourth renunciant, are found." Master Cháng Bǎi: outside traditions have no eightfold path and none of these four — not even a path-corrupter, because only where there is a true path can there be its corruption.

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of brāhmaṇa, and how broad does Master Cháng Bǎi say "brāhmaṇa of true conduct" is?
options: by caste, in name, by true conduct; strictly arhats, broadly all noble ones from the first fruit
quiz.why: "Brāhmaṇa by caste, brāhmaṇa in name only, and brāhmaṇa of true conduct." Master Cháng Bǎi: strictly, only one who has attained arhatship is a brāhmaṇa of true conduct; more broadly, all noble ones from the first fruit up may be so called.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi map the three kinds of holy life to discipline, concentration, and wisdom?
options: keeping precepts is undertaking abstention, succeeding in concentration is temporary cessation, cutting affliction by wisdom is final cessation
quiz.why: "Undertaking abstention, temporary cessation, and final cessation." Master Cháng Bǎi: keeping precepts is the holy life of undertaking abstention; succeeding in concentration is temporary cessation; succeeding in cutting affliction through wisdom is final cessation.
